messages:
maya_cs: putting together a tiny customer-facing one-pager called 'Launch Quickpass' that explains a simple pattern: warmup (prefill) + conservative batching + streaming to reduce cold-start risk and surface renewal signals. Need buy-in on defaults and a tiny paste-ready config + script. quick pls.

sam_sre: sounds good. keep defaults cautious for Hosted. include a circuit-breaker example and telemetry to watch.

owen_se: add an optional prefill window (24-72h) for heavy templates and a line about when to scale batch sizes for Dedicated.

rachel_csm: include renewal heuristics: drop in daily active sessions >20% in first 7d, or >10% increase in support tickets -> outreach. and a 5-item handoff checklist for AMs.

maya_cs: draft paste-ready config (hosted defaults):

```yaml
launch_quickpass:
  prefill_ttl_secs: 3600      # 1h per key, conservative
  kv_prefill: true
  batch:
    enabled: true
    max_batch_size: 12
    max_wait_ms: 100
  streaming:
    enabled: true
    min_tokens_to_stream: 6
  circuit_breaker:
    error_rate_threshold: 0.10
    cooldown_secs: 240
```

sam_sre: good. add operator warmup script to hit 3 canonical prompts once per minute over 30m:

```bash
# warmup Quickpass
prompts=("welcome email" "summary digest" "faq reply")
for p in "${prompts[@]}"; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"open-rl-small","input":"'$p'","prefill":true}' &
done
sleep 1800
```

owen_se: telemetry to list in the one-pager (day0-day7): token/sec, p95 latency, cache hit rate (target >65% after warmup), batch size median, streaming fallback %.

rachel_csm: handoff checklist for AMs (short):
- confirm model & quantization
- expected session RPM and pilot window
- provide 3 eval prompts + quality owner
- set renewal-alert thresholds with CS
- escalation contact (oncall + AM)

maya_cs: short customer-facing note: "During launch warmup (usually up to 48h) we run small, targeted requests to warm caches. You may see slightly higher latency and costs during this window. Your CSM will monitor and adjust settings; if performance or adoption falls short, we'll pause warmup and revert conservative settings while we investigate."

sam_sre: troubleshooting cheats: cache hit rate <40% -> verify prefix keys and prefill jobs; p95 >800ms -> reduce max_batch_size or lower max_wait_ms; error rate above threshold -> open CB and notify oncall.

rachel_csm: include feedback link in emails: https://forms.redwood.example/launch-feedback -> auto-tag critical responses as renewal-risk for AM queue.

maya_cs: I'll draft the one-pager and push a small PR. targeting EOD. cc @deploy-bot for PR job.
